intention: Replace charging's hardcoded 62.0 kWh pack capacity with a real, measured value per vehicle. A monthly job pools each vehicle's valid charge records (USER manual entries and DONE supercharger sessions only), drops small-delta rows, and stores the median as effective_capacity_kwh in a new analytics.vehicle_monthly_metrics table keyed on tesla_id + effective_period. charging reads it back through a port it declares itself, so no Go import cycle. The table is wide, built to hold future monthly metrics as new columns (Linear MAG-32).
request: /kkpa-pickup-linear-ticket MAG-32 — Vehicle Monthly Metrics - New table. Estimate effective capacity per vehicle from MAG-25's inferred_capacity_calc. On the first day of every month, after the nightly job, a named process reads all NOT NULL inferred_capacity_calc values from manual_charge_entries and charge_sessions for the previous month, for every active vehicle, and computes a robust weighted/filtered estimate rather than a simple average. The process may also run for one specific period and one specific tesla id, exposed as an API. effective_capacity will be read by the charging module. Future monthly metrics expected: full_charge_count, average consumption per 100 km, energy consumed per date. Create a KB named vehicle-monthly-metrics.

decisions.decision: charging consumes effective_capacity in this roadmap, through a PackCapacityReader interface charging declares itself; analytics satisfies it structurally and cmd/ wires it. internal/charging imports nothing from internal/analytics. Supersedes backlog #18.
decisions.why: analytics already imports charging, so importing back is a Go compile error. Inverting the dependency is the only wiring that compiles and it keeps module ownership intact.

decisions.decision: Valid input is manual entries with energy_source = 'USER' and supercharger sessions with status = 'DONE'. ESTIMATED entries and DONE_CALCULATED / IN_PROGRESS sessions are excluded.
decisions.why: Those rows had their energy or start percentage derived from the 62.0 constant, so their inferred capacity is exactly 62.0. Including them averages the constant back into itself.

decisions.decision: The estimate is the median of valid rows, after dropping any row whose battery delta is under minDeltaPct. minSamples = 3 and minDeltaPct = 15 are Go constants, never database values.
decisions.why: Capacity error scales as 1/delta, so small charges are noise and are dropped rather than corrected. Median ignores an outlier with no outlier maths. Constants keep tuning migration-free.

decisions.decision: Under minSamples valid rows, effective_capacity_kwh stays NULL. The reader takes the newest measured row at or before the requested period; with no row at all, charging keeps its 62.0.
decisions.why: A stored number then always means measured, never guessed. Pack capacity changes slowly, so last month's measurement is a good answer for a thin month.

decisions.decision: The table has no account_id and is keyed on (tesla_id, effective_period). The job groups vehicles by tesla_id first and pools every owning account's rows into one sample set.
decisions.why: Capacity belongs to the battery pack, not the account. vehicles is UNIQUE (account_id, tesla_id), so a shared car would otherwise make the stored value depend on processing order.

decisions.decision: The trigger is step 4 of app's ProcessVehicleData, after step 3 analytics, running only on the first day of the month and computing the previous month. It follows the existing step-1 short-circuit.
decisions.why: Makes the ticket's 'must run after the nightly job' true by construction rather than by timing. No second scheduler is introduced.

decisions.decision: The month boundary is read through internal/clock in America/Bogota. effective_period is a DATE holding the first day of the month.
decisions.why: The project rule allows no raw time.Now(), no hardcoded zone and no hand-rolled UTC midnight. make tz-guard enforces it.

decisions.decision: The manual re-run surface is cmd/monthly-metrics with -tesla-id and -period flags. internal/gateway is not touched by this roadmap.
decisions.why: The job is run while debugging or backfilling, not from a screen. An HTTP endpoint would add auth and a JSON error shape for a caller that is only the owner.

decisions.decision: No automatic and no SQL backfill. Past periods are computed by running the tool, wrapped in a make cmd-monthly-metrics target following the Makefile's existing cmd-* convention.
decisions.why: Reuses the tool tier 4 already builds, so backfill costs no extra code. A SQL backfill would write the estimator a second time where it cannot be unit-tested.

decisions.decision: One name everywhere: table analytics.vehicle_monthly_metrics, port MonthlyMetricsCalculator, runnable cmd/monthly-metrics, target make cmd-monthly-metrics, KB vehicle-monthly-metrics. No synonyms.
decisions.why: An agent that reads any one of the five names can guess the other four. The name still fits when future monthly metrics arrive.

decisions.decision: Database design gate PASSED. Wide table, one row per vehicle-month, one nullable column per metric plus its sample count. UNIQUE (tesla_id, effective_period) serves the single read path; no separate CREATE INDEX. No FK, no raw_data.
decisions.why: sqlc gives typed fields, reads need no pivot, units keep their _kwh suffix, and the DDL lists the whole vocabulary. Mirrors vehicle_metrics' own index reasoning.
